statusContract.supported: The named slice has an implementation, an external entry point, and matching automated evidence.
statusContract.partial: Some implementation or validation exists, but the acceptance boundary is not closed.
statusContract.planned: The remaining implementation or execution is scheduled and is not delivered.
statusContract.not_planned: The capability is explicitly outside the current SonnetDB contract.
statusContract.beta: A bounded preview contract is available; production gates are not passed.

capabilities.name: Time-series database
capabilities.boundary: The default millisecond engine uses single-Point WAL v2 atomic recovery, catalog v2 downgrade barriers, bounded recovery, rotation/checkpoint/flush, cancellation and unknown-result reconciliation. Public API multi-field recovery and deterministic process-kill boundaries are verified locally; WriteMany is not a whole-batch atomic unit. Default operating-system flush/per-write-fsync settings, KEEP_ALL and global TTL are unchanged. T2/T3 partition/duplicate decisions and M50 per-database us/ns remain separate. Original-scale, physical power-loss, fixed-hardware and long-run gates remain open.

capabilities.name: Relational SQL
capabilities.boundary: Current shared-LSM tables implement one atomic WAL batch for rows, indexes, per-table sequences and persisted row counts, plus consolidated maintenance metadata. Only transactions within the same shared store use this path; mixed legacy/standalone/shared layouts retain the recovery journal. The practical SQL subset, migrations, JSON updates and OwnsMany have implemented slices with scoped historical consumer evidence. Consult the current SQL contract for exact syntax and type support rather than stale individual issue lists. Full query working-set bounds, mixed-layout fault coverage, original-scale concurrency/performance and field recovery remain separate gates; EF application NativeAOT is not established by Server AOT.

capabilities.name: Persistent key-value
capabilities.boundary: Current source defaults to LSM with automatic legacy migration. K7 functional integration is implemented; MANIFEST v2 now prevents a real pre-K6 LSM reader/writer from bypassing generation v3 guards. Migration/rollback persistence boundaries, isolated space/partial-write/sync/unknown faults, complete values/versions/TTL/counts/indexes, pinned SST reclamation and real historical binary rejection are locally verified. KvWriteBufferManager remains a soft budget. Original-scale capacity, randomized crash scale, full physical write-amplification/cold-I/O/fsync/TTL/TRUNCATE measurements, fixed hardware and long runs remain separate gates. Historical performance gains, regressions and unknown failure causes are retained.

capabilities.name: JSON document store
capabilities.boundary: The documented single-node subset and opt-in cumulative materialization admission for direct raw document SQL including TTL and single result-name ORDER BY are locally supported. Direct vector_search and JSON-file TVF cumulative materialization admission is also locally supported in its bounded scalar subset. Other multi-column blocking/search/nested document budget paths, overall heap limits, remote budget options, MongoDB wire compatibility and million/ten-million capacity remain outside this slice or unverified.

capabilities.name: Full-text search
capabilities.boundary: Embedded, Server and source remote SDK typed paths perform complete bounded filtering before scoring/sort/pagination, preserving exact TotalHits and full filtered-set facets. Shared time/work/total-response-byte budgets cover scanning/postings, sorting, facets, projection, source-generated JSON and transport; failures return no consumable partial result. Local 10003-document field parity, independent sort oracles and separate real Server/consumer processes are verified. Continuations read the current view rather than a cross-page snapshot. External remote hosts, a new public NuGet consumer, relevance quality, cross-request merge working sets and original-scale capacity remain separate gates.

capabilities.name: Vector search
capabilities.boundary: Exact fallback, bounded Top-K, VECTOR parameter binding and REST/NDJSON float[] transport are locally implemented; Core 3/3 and Kestrel REST 2/2 pass. Remote Frame E2E, generic filtered ANN, Recall@K, quality and fixed-hardware evidence remain open.

capabilities.name: Object and content storage
capabilities.boundary: Bucket, version, range, multipart and transfer contracts exist; fixed-hardware, large-file crash recovery and complete backup evidence remain open.

capabilities.name: Persistent log and message queue
capabilities.boundary: Publish/batch/pull/ACK, replay, delivery governance, instance snapshots and offline snapshot/inspect/restore CLI are implemented. Defaults flush to the operating system without per-publish fsync. Database backup does not include instance MQ; coordinated recovery with database data, identities/configuration, external objects and derived state remains a separate gate. At-least-once delivery does not promise distributed transactions, arbitrary business exactly-once or physical power-loss acceptance.

capabilities.name: Native property graph
capabilities.boundary: Graph Beta also supports opt-in cumulative row/estimated-byte admission for direct native node/edge and fixed one-hop scalar SQL. Snapshot/pages and transient decode allocations remain independent; overall heap/first-row, external comparison, fixed hardware and long-run gates remain open.

capabilities.name: Spatial, geography and trajectory
capabilities.boundary: Geospatial values and industrial entry points exist; cross-model permissions, scale and a complete real-device journey remain to be verified.

capabilities.name: Stream processing and subscriptions
capabilities.boundary: A bounded local file subscription persists events, watermark, in-flight delivery, pause, conditional retry and explicit exhausted-batch DLQ quarantine with recoverable checkpoint coordination. Persistent UTC tumbling and bounded-overlap sliding COUNT and exact decimal numeric windows also support opt-in Ordinal string grouping, bounded groups/results and composite-cursor pagination while preserving legacy states. Local composed checks reconcile commit-before-ACK replay and explicit new window baselines after quarantine; existing windows reject skipped checkpoints. DLQ replay persists a stable consumer replay identity and conditionally deletes completed records without reusing sequence numbers. Local composed checks cover replay recovery and sliding commit-before-ACK deduplication. Persistent session COUNT and task catalogs, bounded automatic delivery with non-overlapping timed-out handlers, and dedicated single-partition CDC-to-stream outbox/receipt recovery are locally implemented. Unknown target publication after premature consumer reclamation fails closed for manual recovery handoff. Business side-effect transactions, remote parity, field recovery and distributed semantics remain open.

capabilities.name: CDC, edge synchronization and replication
capabilities.boundary: Versioned codec/spool, real document change-feed capture, fixed read views and snapshot replicas support local resume; an explicit bounded topology fairly advances up to 64 independently committed partitions. A dedicated single-partition outbox/target-receipt bridge now persists delivery proof before source ACK. Callers must restore pending bridge intents before consumption and supply correctly sourced dedicated spools. Cross-directory business and cross-partition transactions, remote transport, offline synchronization, conflict/schema policy, client routes and field evidence remain open.

capabilities.name: Multimodal AI and RAG
capabilities.boundary: Provider, Copilot, image search and durable RAG contracts exist. BrowserDirect OAuth and StudioNative host-held credentials/chat have verified local contracts; real-model quality/cost, deployed dual-network journeys, live multi-instance takeover and field recovery evidence remain open.

capabilities.name: Governance, backup, recovery, observability and security
capabilities.boundary: Authentication, per-database authorization, audit, health, metrics, local budgets and database backup are implemented. SQL admission, Frame/MCP response budgets and KV soft write-buffer limits have separate scopes and do not establish a hard process-wide resource ceiling. Full instance recovery must explicitly include database data, instance MQ, identity/configuration, external objects and applicable derived state. Cross-architecture release, clean installation, physical power loss and long-run acceptance remain separate from source and CI evidence.
